Super Kalium / SDK receiving audit

One event stream.
Three handling paths.

A source-level comparison of develop, this branch’s main-app SDK session, and the Notification Service Extension. Includes server events, nested message actions, feature configuration and transport behavior.

Baseline develop @ 6800d16349 · Branch mo/nse-incremental-rebuild @ 86a1f722a3
2026-09-07 23:38:27 +0200 · fix(nse): defer conversation clears and preserve app behavior
Generated 2026-09-08 03:01 UTC · Latest committed snapshot · Uncommitted changes excluded

What matters most

  • Ordinary calls now use AVS after notification processing. Call candidates can come from the entire processed prefix. Host CallKit reporting requires the supplied Swift helper; processed markers do not provide a retry for this later presentation work.
  • NSE clear signals save CLEAR_CONVERSATION_CONTENT or DELETE_CONVERSATION_LOCALLY in the existing PendingActions table. Content, files and MLS state remain intact. The app deliberately leaves these actions pending without executing or acknowledging them.
  • The app starts self-delete timers through its deletion handler; the NSE persists a receive-time deadline. Only the app performs timer-driven deletion.
  • Full feature refresh now propagates handler failures instead of reporting success after skipped writes. Earlier successful writes are not rolled back as a group.
  • File cleanup can now block app conversation deletion. The main-app filter includes changes inside delegated use cases, as well as direct handlers.
  • NSE typing, remote mute, in-call emoji, unknown property updates and mapped unknown feature variants are explicit no-ops. Unknown outer event types and several native or lifecycle cases can still block processing.
  • Pending proposals are handed to the app scheduler through native state and SQL deadlines. The NSE does not send due commits or process their responses.
  • Legal-hold user events are consumed without applying the app’s legal-hold effects. They are not left pending for later app handling.

How to read this map

Latest committed snapshot: the branch comparison uses 86a1f722a3. Uncommitted changes are excluded. Later commits need an audit refresh; this document is not a live monitor.

Every row compares behavior, not just file placement. “Shared rules” can still have different failure handling, transaction boundaries or alert policy. Read the NSE conditions and notes before inferring parity.

When canonical NSE processing throws before completion, that notification’s processed marker remains unset and the later queue waits. Earlier completed notifications remain processed. Explicit no-ops advance the marker. AVS evaluation and host CallKit reporting happen after these markers; failures at that later stage do not undo processing or arrange a presentation retry.

Supported persistence does not imply an alert. Text presentation uses only the target notification’s last eligible candidate, subject to privacy and final stored state. Incoming-call presentation can instead use an AVS result from any notification processed before or at the target.

This is a static code audit, not a new execution of the SDK tests or a claim of production readiness. Existing fixture references are evidence pointers; their reported results were not rerun for this document.

Where events actually run

develop · app session

WebSocket / REST → EventDataSource↓ map stored payloadsEventMapper → EventProcessor↓ domain receivers and handlersRepositories / crypto / app effects

Gathered-batch crypto boundary. No public :nse receiver at this revision.

Current branch · app session

WebSocket / REST → EventDataSource↓ same receiving graphEventMapper → EventProcessor↓ shared rules + app handlersRepositories / crypto / app effects

Retains app orchestration. Page storage, payload identities and some failure paths changed.

Current branch · NSE

KaliumNSEReceiver → owned account↓ REST / pending queue up to targetNotificationProcessor → ReceivedPayload↓ NotificationEffects / ReceivedMessageHandlerSQL → native commits → processed marker

Per-notification canonical work, then text selection and AVS evaluation. The receiver budget is capped at 25 seconds; cleanup can extend return time. Host CallKit reporting follows the receiver.

REST pages / queue orderPipeline & transportSeparate pathPending fetch filters out null payloads, removes overlapping unprocessed live rows, inserts events and updates last-saved ID through separate calls. Cancellation uses isActive in the loop.EventDataSource propagates cursor/page storage failures, checks cancellation and rejects an empty page with hasMore. EventDAO.storeFetchedPage atomically removes overlapping unprocessed live rows, inserts non-null payloads and saves the last non-transient cursor. Null-payload filtering is unchanged.
Behavior changedPending pages now store atomically with their cursor and propagate storage/cancellation failures. Null payloads are still filtered before insertion.
NotificationEventStore atomically stores whole REST pages, including null/transient payload rows, with the last non-transient fetch cursor. NotificationProcessor consumes the stored pending prefix through the target. Null/empty payloads block during processing; repeated/overlapping pages or a missing target fail the attempt.

The cursor records fetched non-transient history, not completion. A transient suffix never becomes the next REST cursor; an all-transient page leaves the cursor unchanged. Successful earlier notifications may be marked processed before a later one blocks.

SQL / crypto / processed markerPipeline & transportSeparate pathA gathered app batch runs inside the crypto transaction with database invalidations muted. Handler-specific writes are not one whole-batch SQL transaction. Processed IDs are saved after transaction success.Retains the gathered-batch crypto boundary, muted database invalidations and handler-specific SQL writes. Returned handler/flush failures now throw inside the crypto callback; this only covers failures actually returned or thrown by handlers. Metadata Flow reads retain the configured dispatcher.
Behavior changedHandler failures now throw inside the crypto transaction; metadata reads stay on their configured dispatcher.
Each notification runs Proteus → optional MLS → decode → one SQL effects transaction → native commits → processed marker. SQL preference/configuration reads use the writer dispatcher. Call events are evaluated by AVS after all prefix/target markers have been saved.

SQL, native stores, files, HTTP effects and processed markers are separate commits. Canonical failures before the marker leave that event pending; replay protections vary by event. Later AVS evaluation or host CallKit failure does not roll markers back. Database invalidation muting in the app is not a whole-batch SQL transaction.

Prepared account / cancellation / feature policiesPipeline & transportSeparate pathNormal app sessions own their repositories and background processing; no public NSE receiver exists.Apple session provider coordinates account ownership and publishes/revokes receiving readiness. The regular app batch remains NonCancellable. Apple call-manager teardown now joins its jobs and fails if a native AVS handle was requested, because native callback teardown is unavailable.
Behavior changedApple app sessions now coordinate account leases and publish or revoke NSE receiving readiness. Apple calling teardown now joins jobs and rejects native-handle release without callback teardown.
Requires compatible prepared account state, an exclusive account lease and matching build switches. Public work budget is 1–25,000 ms; native callbacks restore cancellation. Proxy configurations/credentials and Nomad-prepared receiving are rejected. MLS commit sends remain forbidden; pending proposals are left for the app scheduler. AVS evaluation is inside the receiving attempt; the Swift host reports CallKit after receiver completion.

Readiness, ownership or budget can prevent any event family from running. Resource draining/close runs during teardown and is not a guarantee of an exact wall-clock completion deadline. CoreCrypto uses its available open API after file checks; this audit does not certify strict native no-create/no-migration opening. An app AVS teardown failure prevents a normal ownership handoff to NSE; the native-handle guard explicitly requires retaining account ownership until process exit.

Alert selection / retriesPipeline & transportSeparate pathApp GetNotificationsUseCase observes regular and ephemeral notification flows and maps local notification records.Retains the app notification observation flow; shared receiving writes can be read by the app after reopening.
No identified changeThe app notification observation and mapping flow is unchanged; event-specific persistence changes are classified separately.
Message presentation is target-only and chooses its last eligible candidate from final stored state. Calling payloads from the entire processed prefix through the target are accumulated and evaluated together by AVS after markers commit. The facade returns incoming/missed/closed call results; host code must include and await the Swift CallKit helper. Preview names/text obey privacy and verification gating.

An already processed target returns silent success with no call replay. AVS processing-result failures are logged as best effort, while thrown failures/cancellation can fail the facade after events are already marked processed. CallKit reporting is a separate host operation; neither messages nor calls have durable missed-presentation recovery here.

Modern feature configuration refreshPipeline & transportSeparate pathFeatureConfigEventReceiver is deprecated. SyncFeatureConfigsUseCase fetches configuration and invokes handlers including channels, consumable notifications and apps; UserConfigSyncWorker periodically invokes it.Keeps periodic/full configuration refresh but now returns the first handler failure instead of ignoring handler Eithers and reporting success. Behavior changedFull feature refresh now propagates handler failures and stops subsequent handlers, including channel storage failures, instead of reporting success after skipped writes.
No full feature-sync worker in the bounded receiver. Consumes prepared/persisted configuration and handles supported arriving feature DTOs through NotificationEffects and ReceivedMLSConfigurationHandler.

Feature rows describe incoming legacy feature-event dispatch as well as handler rules; many legacy event branches remain no-ops even when modern refresh applies that setting. Refresh is sequential, not an atomic configuration transaction.

conversation.create / NewConversationDTOConversationSeparate pathPersists conversation and members, resolves one-to-one protocol, updates modification time, loads unknown users, and generates creation/unverified/member/receipt/apps/Cells system messages for a newly handled conversation.Same orchestration, with extracted shared conversation mapping and createForEvent system-message rules.
Refactor onlyConversation mapping and the same creation-message sequence move to shared helpers; the main app keeps its existing identities and best-effort handling.
Stages metadata, members and profiles, invokes shared creation system-message rules with deterministic IDs, and resolves the lifecycle only for ONE_ON_ONE conversations before one SQL write. The creation mapper accepts CONNECTION_PENDING alongside group, one-to-one and self types. Creation alone produces no notification candidate.

Pending-connection creation no longer fails solely because its mapped type is CONNECTION_PENDING; this permits a paired pending user.connection / conversation.create notification to finish if all remaining effects succeed. Compatible lifecycle, self membership and MLS metadata/replay guards still apply. Creation and welcome cooperate to avoid restoring stale members. One-to-one resolution requires an available compatible target; it does not create or externally join a missing MLS target.

conversation.delete / DeletedConversationDTOConversationGap / conditionalDeletes through DeleteConversationUseCase; after success schedules an ephemeral conversation-deleted notification except for meetings; invokes the persistence deletion hook even if lookup fails.The event handler is unchanged, but DeleteConversationUseCase now deletes conversation asset/draft files before deleting local conversation and native MLS state. File-cleanup failure stops that deletion path; successful non-meeting deletion still schedules the app notification.
Behavior changedDeleteConversationUseCase now removes conversation asset/draft files before SQL/native deletion; cleanup failure prevents deletion and its notification. The outer event handler itself is unchanged.
Deletes existing Proteus conversation/files and returns CONVERSATION_DELETED candidate; meeting deletion has shouldNotify=false. Missing conversation is a no-op. Explicitly blocks MLS-capable deletion and deletion/recreation or earlier dependent effects in one notification.

Safe Proteus deletes work in NSE; MLS-capable deletion remains app-owned because native replay cannot retain deleted-group identity. NSE omits the persistence hook. The app invokes that hook in both the successful deletion use case and the outer handler; the outer hook still runs after lookup or deletion failure. Earlier required effects, including member-role updates, can prevent NSE deletion.

Same sender/self-carrier authorization; upserts CLEAR_CONVERSATION_CONTENT for the target with the backend message receive timestamp. The pending action commits with the notification’s SQL effects. Messages, assets, files, delivery work and presentation candidates stay intact.

 224     private suspend fun trackingIdentifier(unpacked: MessageUnpackResult.ApplicationMessage, content: MessageContent.DataTransfer) {

Calling / ordinary AVS payload and host CallKit presentationMessage contentSeparate pathNon-REMOTEMUTE types forward to live CallManager.onCallingMessageReceived.Same live CallManager routing for non-REMOTEMUTE payloads, with only self devices allowed to redirect the calling conversation.
No identified changeOrdinary calling payloads still route through the same live CallManager handler.
Decodes JSON and collects authorized target/sender/client/time/protocol call events in SQL order. After processing the pending prefix through the target and marking events complete, AppleCallingEvents passes the batch to AVS and returns incoming, missed and closed results. The optional host KaliumNSECallKitReporter reports incoming calls to CallKit and stops only rings reported earlier in that request.

Host must include and invoke the Swift reporter; SDK processing alone does not call CallKit. AVS processing failures are logged as best effort. Call evaluation/reporting is after event markers, so retry of an already-processed target returns no calls. Caller names are suppressed for degraded verification. No live app CallManager, call-history row or separate missed-call OS alert is created by this NSE branch.

Refactor onlyFederation member-selection and system-message factories are shared while app deletion effects, random IDs and failure handling remain the same.
Remove cross-domain connection requests and local files; mark one-to-one peers defederated while retaining history; remove selected group members and create stopped/member-removal messages. Deterministic IDs and retained messages drive canonical replay; SQL/file failure or conflicting required/recreated metadata aborts. No direct content.

Stored federation system messages do not create an NSE banner. Replay validates canonical sender/content and restores group selection from retained removal-message members.

Coverage and provenance

The inventory was checked against the declared wire event names, all FeatureConfigData variants, and the application-message dispatcher. Nested cases have separate rows where behavior differs. System messages generated as effects are described with their triggering event; they are not counted as independent incoming wire events.

Scope: SDK incoming notification/sync events and decrypted application-message handling, plus the transport controls that deliver them. UI interaction callbacks, outbound request handlers, database observation callbacks, native AVS callbacks and full-sync jobs are outside the wire-event inventory; relevant app-only hooks and prerequisites are noted in the comparison.

Important adjacent receiving paths
  • The deprecated FeatureConfigEventReceiver says feature events are no longer sent; modern configuration refresh uses SyncFeatureConfigsUseCase and UserConfigSyncWorker. The matrix documents event behavior if these DTOs arrive, not the entire configuration-refresh lifecycle.
  • LocalEventManager sends API-response events through the same EventProcessor; it does not add a separate wire family. NSE proposal state and deadlines are handed to the app scheduler; the NSE does not send commits or recursively decode commit responses.
  • Ordinary Calling payloads are accumulated across the processed prefix and evaluated through AVS after notification markers are written. The host integrates KaliumNSECallKitReporter.swift to report an incoming call after the receiver returns; remote mute and in-call emoji are consumed without their live-app effects.
